newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures close higher after strong rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures close higher after strong rally.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher after the market staged a strong technical upside breakout on continued signs that U.S. inflation remains low, traders said.

An article in the July 14 edition of Business Week set the backdrop for such sentiment, suggesting U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan appears more tolerant of faster growth and lower unemployment than in the past.
Greenspan believes the U.S. economy is going through a dramatic change in productivity, and he thinks statistical aberrations understate increases in efficiency, the article said.
"They (the Fed) are hitting the nail on the head in assessing the larger macroeconomic forces," one debt market analyst said.

The Business Week article was released on the heels of U.S. June labor data, released during Thursday's short pre-holiday session, that showed the pace of job growth was slowing from the first quarter.

Any fears that inflationary pressures would emerge from the commodity markets were dashed as COMEX gold prices fell to 12-year lows, contributing to a decline of nearly 1.5 percent in the Commodity Research Bureau Index.
Traders and analysts noted the Reserve Bank of Australia's sale of 167 tonnes of gold -- more than two-thirds of its holdings -- over the past six months.
Gold prices, which were already trading near four-year lows, collapsed in early-morning trade, and helped spur September T-bonds above Friday's high of 113-15/32, they said.
Locals and dealers were caught short several times during the day, as many had been anticipating pullbacks before further advances.
However, profit-taking emerged only in the last hour of the day, several traders said.

About four firms, including one German-based house, sold a total of 3,500 September T-bonds late in the day, floor sources said. The contract slipped through support at 113-24/32 and now faces near-term support at 113-16/32.
The 113-16/32 level, which represents a trendline from 1996, was a resistance level at the start of the day.
September T-bonds spiked to 113-24/32, above the December 9 high of 113-19/32, before midsession on heavy volume, and steadily inched to a fresh seven-month high of 113-31/32.
December Eurodollars rose to 94.08, and closed only five basis points higher than March.

Stephanie Davis, a money market analyst at Technical Data, said the spread first narrowed to five basis points on Friday, July 4, for the tightest spread this year. In April, the spread between the lead contract month and March was about 30 basis points.

At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds were up 15/32 at 113-21/32, 10-year T-notes were 08/32 higher at 109-12/32, and December Eurodollars were 0.015 higher at 94.06. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
